routing_warnings.description: The request to assess whether images fit the book's tone and color palette belongs to chapter-image editorial fit rather than manuscript prose polishing.
The missing updates from the client's latest source file concern integration of client-authored revisions.
The corner artifacts and partially cropped chapter images concern image placement and quality.
The request to italicize text under Mama's Hot Take belongs to its dedicated styling Requirement.
The request for lighter pages and more paragraph spacing belongs to page density and spacing.
The instruction to use a particular authoritative file belongs to client revision integration.
The claim that all three client-listed source-file changes were completed primarily concerns integration of client revisions.
The question about author-name placement on the first page concerns title-page layout.
The page-number and table-of-contents requests belong to pagination and TOC.
The chapter-title and subtitle formatting requests belong to chapter-heading formatting.
The requirement to place an image at the beginning of every chapter concerns image placement rather than editorial suitability.
The elongated and cropped chapter-image observations are technical rendering failures rather than editorial-fit evidence.
The full-page image decision concerns technical image layout.
The request to check for pixelation concerns image rendering quality.
The corner artifacts and partially cropped chapter images are technical placement and rendering failures.
The client selects the book's 5.5 by 8.5 inch trim size; the dedicated trim-size Requirement is the narrower target.

The freelancer's claim about improving flow, removing repetition, and publication readiness primarily reports completion of manuscript editorial work rather than a distinct execution transition for publishing guidance.
The request to check the manuscript for repeated full stops is a general punctuation-proofreading instruction rather than a change to the authoritative revision source.
The freelancer's removal claim resolves the punctuation-proofreading request in message 168 and is better routed to editorial polish.
The request to review the Table of Contents belongs to the separate Table of Contents Requirement.
The message asks for review of which supplied images fit their labeled chapters rather than changing technical placement.
The message selects the illustration for the GiftingRight chapter rather than changing its technical placement.
The requested review concerns thematic fit and colour-palette consistency.
The observed elongated and cropped images are rendering-quality failures covered by the narrower Requirement.
Avoiding pixelation is a rendering-quality constraint rather than a placement change.
Corner artifacts and partially cropped chapter images are concrete rendering-quality failures.
The instruction to place an image at the beginning of every chapter concerns image placement rather than rendering quality.
The selection of full-page images concerns placement and sizing treatment rather than rendering quality.
This message specifically concerns updating page-number references in the table of contents rather than adding interior page numbers.
The full-page image-placement decision is independent of the paperback trim-size decision.
The freelancer's implementation claim concerns full-page chapter-image placement, not paperback trim size.
